stem:
Meena fixes four small nails to a straight copper rod with drops of melted wax. Nail P is 2 cm from one end of the rod, nail Q is 6 cm from that end, nail R is 10 cm away, and nail S is 14 cm away. She holds that end of the rod in the flame of a kitchen gas stove.
As heat passes along the rod by conduction, in which order do the nails drop off?

options.text: All four nails drop off together as soon as the rod is heated
S, then R, then Q, then P
P, then Q, then R, then S
Q, then P, then S, then R

teacher.key_rationale: In conduction through a solid, heat is transferred particle to particle from the hot end toward colder parts, so the wax nearest the flame melts first and the nails fall in order of increasing distance from the flame: P (2 cm), Q (6 cm), R (10 cm), S (14 cm). Option C is correct. Option A is the trap for a student who treats the whole rod as heating at once; B reverses the direction of heat flow; D is a scrambled order.
